description:
**Problem**

`bd admin doctor` reports a false `index_offsets` failure that escalates the
whole store to `risk=high safe_to_accept_writes=false safe_to_prune_wal=false`,
on a store that is completely healthy.

```
- index_offsets: fail (severity=high, issues=3)
    * index_offset_invalid: failed to open wal segment: No such file or directory
      (os error 2) path=wal/core/segment-1785401979420-e57701ef-....wal
```

The segment file exists. The reported `path` is **relative**, and it is passed
straight to `File::open`, so it resolves against the daemon's current working
directory instead of the store data dir.

Proof:

- Daemon cwd: `/home/darin/src/personal/beads-rs` (whatever repo triggered autostart)
- Real file: `~/.local/share/beads-rs/stores/<id>/wal/core/segment-...wal` (present)
- `bd admin rebuild-index` on the same store: `segments_scanned: 2, records_indexed: 3`
  -- the WAL reader opens those exact segments fine
- `wal_frames` and `wal_hashes` both **pass**, because they scan via
  `SegmentInfo.path` from the filesystem walker, which is absolute
- Repair loop is useless: `maintenance on` -> `rebuild-index` -> doctor still fails,
  because nothing was ever wrong

**Root cause**

`wal.sqlite` stores `segment_path` relative to the store root
(`crates/beads-daemon-core/src/wal/index.rs`, `SegmentRow::segment_path()` in
`crates/beads-daemon-core/src/wal/mod.rs:584`).

`scrub_index_offsets` in `crates/beads-daemon/src/runtime/scrubber.rs:694`
builds `segment_paths` directly from `segment.segment_path().to_path_buf()` and
`verify_index_offset` then does `File::open(&path)` (~line 829) with no join
against the store root. Compare `scan_segment_records` (~line 371), which opens
`SegmentInfo.path` and works.

**Impact**

No data is at risk and writes are unaffected (verified: `bd create` succeeds
while `safe_to_accept_writes=false`). But the health surface lies, the
recommended repair action never clears it, and anything gating automation on
`risk` or `safe_to_accept_writes` will misfire.

**Design**

1. Resolve index-reported segment paths against the store root before opening.
   Prefer doing it once where `segment_paths` is built in `scrub_index_offsets`,
   so `verify_index_offset` keeps taking ready-to-open paths.
2. Better: make the type carry the truth. Have the index reader return paths
   already resolved against the store root, so a relative `segment_path` cannot
   escape the persistence layer. That kills the whole class rather than this
   one call site.
3. Audit other `segment_path()` consumers for the same relative-path assumption.

**Acceptance**

- [ ] `bd admin doctor` reports `index_offsets: pass` on a healthy store regardless of daemon cwd
- [ ] Regression test running the scrubber with a daemon cwd different from the store root
- [ ] No remaining `File::open` of an unresolved index-sourced `segment_path`
- [ ] `cargo xtest` green

**Files:** `crates/beads-daemon/src/runtime/scrubber.rs`,
`crates/beads-daemon-core/src/wal/index.rs`, `crates/beads-daemon-core/src/wal/mod.rs`
title: bd admin doctor falsely reports index_offsets failure (relative segment path opened against daemon cwd)

description:
**Problem**
`crates/beads-rs/src/test_harness/mod.rs` is a 1.6k-line daemon/repl/WAL/network simulation harness that currently lives under the assembly crate even though its consumers are not assembly internals. The audit for `beads-rs-gou3.7.3` shows that `crates/beads-rs/tests/e2e.rs` is the only consumer of `beads_rs::test_harness`, so this surface should move to the daemon-owned testkit instead of keeping a broad subsystem harness under `beads-rs`.

**Why It Matters**
As long as the e2e harness lives under `beads-rs`, opening the assembly crate still drags in daemon runtime/store/WAL/repl concerns and weakens local reasoning about crate ownership.

**Design**
- Move the reusable e2e support types from `crates/beads-rs/src/test_harness/mod.rs` into `crates/beads-daemon/src/testkit/e2e.rs` (or equivalent daemon-owned testkit surface).
- Expose only the e2e support that `crates/beads-rs/tests/e2e.rs` actually needs: `TestWorld`, `TestNode`, `NodeOptions`, `ReplicationRig`, `Direction`, `NetworkProfile`, `latency_budget_ms`, `replication_latency_budget_ms`, `measure_latency`.
- Update `crates/beads-rs/tests/e2e.rs` to import the lower crate directly.
- Prefer deleting `beads-rs::test_harness` entirely rather than leaving a compat re-export seam.

**Files To Study**
- `crates/beads-rs/src/test_harness/mod.rs`
- `crates/beads-rs/tests/e2e.rs`
- `crates/beads-daemon/src/testkit/mod.rs`
- `crates/beads-daemon/src/lib.rs`

**Acceptance**
- [ ] `crates/beads-rs/tests/e2e.rs` no longer imports `beads_rs::test_harness::*`
- [ ] The moved harness lives under `beads-daemon` testkit ownership
- [ ] `beads-rs` no longer exposes the broad subsystem test harness surface
- [ ] `cargo test -p beads-rs --features e2e-tests --test e2e` passes
- [ ] relevant daemon package checks pass after the move

title: Move e2e harness from beads-rs into beads-daemon testkit
